stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: In the shawl workshops of eighteenth-century Kashmir, a single design was divided among dozens of weavers, each responsible for one narrow strip that would later be stitched invisibly to its neighbors. A finished shawl might pass through a hundred hands. This ______ method of production, historians argue, explains how workshops could fill large orders while keeping each weaver's task simple.
explanation: The phrase "this ______ method" points back to the process just described: one design split into strips that separate weavers make and that are then joined. You need a word meaning "made one part at a time," and "piecemeal" means exactly that. It also fits the claim that the method kept each task simple.

A.why: "Desultory" means aimless or without a plan. The passage describes a carefully coordinated division of labor, so the word clashes with the process you just read about.

B.why: "Peripatetic" means traveling from place to place. It sounds like it could match a shawl passing "through a hundred hands," but the shawl moving between weavers is not the same as the method itself being itinerant. You picked a word that looks like the idea instead of one that means it.

D.why: "Cursory" means hasty and superficial. Strips stitched together "invisibly" show careful work, not rushed work. You may have reached for the familiar word because it seemed to fit roughly.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Wheat farmers have long regarded clover growing between their rows as ______, a weed that robs the crop of water and soil nutrients. Field trials in central Kansas, however, found that plots with a clover understory produced about 8 percent more grain than clover-free plots, apparently because bacteria in the clover's roots fixed nitrogen that the wheat could then absorb.
explanation: The blank sits inside the old view that the trials then overturn. That view calls clover a weed that "robs" the crop, so the blank has to mean harmful. "Deleterious" means damaging, which is precisely that belief.

B.why: "Extraneous" means unnecessary or irrelevant. That fits the general idea of an unwanted weed, but the deciding word is "robs": farmers thought clover actively did damage, not just that it didn't matter. It is close in meaning but not precise.

C.why: "Ubiquitous" means found everywhere. How widespread clover is has nothing to do with the belief the passage describes, which is about harm to the crop.

D.why: "Innocuous" means harmless, which is the opposite of the farmers' view. You may have borrowed the conclusion of the trials and put it into the sentence describing the belief those trials overturn.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Speakers of the Tavani dialects have been notably ______ in their borrowing. Although these communities have traded with Portuguese speakers for roughly three centuries, linguist Ana Beltrão found fewer than forty Portuguese loanwords in a 12,000-word corpus of recorded speech, and nearly all of them named imported tools.
explanation: The next sentence defines the blank: after three centuries of contact there are fewer than forty loanwords, and nearly all of them name specific imported objects. You need a word meaning "sparing and cautious," and "chary" means exactly that. Don't pass over it just because it's less familiar.

A.why: "Indiscriminate" means taking things in without selecting. A handful of loanwords limited to one category shows the opposite of indiscriminate borrowing.

C.why: "Taciturn" means saying little in conversation. It sounds like the idea of holding back words, but the passage is about which words speakers adopt, not how much they talk. You matched a word that sounds right to one with an unrelated meaning.

D.why: "Diffident" means shy or lacking confidence. The data show that speakers borrowed few words but say nothing about their feelings. You went beyond what the corpus can tell you.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Excavators at the Dunmore rock shelter describe its floor as a ______: each band of visitors seems to have swept aside the debris of the last before laying new hearths, so that traces of at least six successive occupations overlap and partially erase one another, forcing researchers to reconstruct earlier layers from the fragments that survived later disturbance.
explanation: The text after the colon defines the label: new layers laid over old ones, partly erasing what came before, with the earlier layers recoverable only from fragments. A "palimpsest" is a surface that has been reused so that earlier traces show through later ones. That is an exact fit.

A.why: "Monolith" suggests something single and uniform. The floor is made of six overlapping occupations, not one unbroken whole.

B.why: "Mosaic" roughly fits because the floor is made of many pieces. But a mosaic sets pieces side by side. The deciding detail is that the layers "overlap and partially erase one another," and a mosaic doesn't capture that. You chose the familiar word that almost fits.

C.why: "Cenotaph" is a monument to someone buried elsewhere. It sounds archaeological, but it has nothing to do with layered occupation debris. You matched the topic instead of the function.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Mediterranean portolan charts of the fourteenth century were drawn for sailors, who needed accurate coastlines and compass bearings far more than information about what lay beyond the shore. Chartmakers therefore treated inland regions ______, often leaving them blank or filling them with a few stylized cities and banners that had little to do with actual geography.
explanation: "Therefore" ties the blank to the chartmakers' priorities. Sailors didn't need the interior, so the interior got little attention: it was left blank or given decoration. "Cursorily" means with quick, superficial attention, which is what follows from that reasoning.

B.why: "Meticulously" means with great care. Blank spaces and decorative cities show the opposite, and the "therefore" logic calls for less attention, not more.

C.why: "Disingenuously" means insincerely or with intent to deceive. The passage says the cities had little to do with real geography, but it gives no evidence that chartmakers meant to mislead anyone. Their reason was simply what sailors needed.

D.why: "Ambivalently" means with mixed or conflicting feelings. It may sound like "vaguely" or "uncertainly," but the passage describes a clear choice about priorities, not divided feelings. You picked a word that resembles the idea you wanted.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: While circling a female, males of one reef cuttlefish species ripple bands of dark pigment down their bodies, raise their front arms into a crest, and flush from mottled brown to brilliant white within seconds. Researchers once assumed that these ______ displays served mainly to warn off rival males, but video analysis shows that males seldom perform them when no female is nearby.
explanation: "These ______ displays" labels the behavior described in the first sentence: rippling pigment, a raised crest, and a flash to brilliant white. That is showy behavior meant to be noticed, and "ostentatious" means conspicuously showy.

A.why: "Ostensible" means apparent or claimed, and it looks and sounds almost like "ostentatious." The blank describes how the displays look, not a purpose that only seems to be true. You were caught by a look-alike word.

C.why: "Cryptic" means concealing, and in biology it often refers to camouflage. A flash to brilliant white is the opposite of concealment. You matched the marine-biology topic instead of the description.

D.why: "Tentative" means hesitant. A male that changes color completely within seconds while circling a female is acting boldly, not tentatively.

adjudication.why: The rippling, cresting, color-flashing behavior is showy, which is what "ostentatious" means; "ostensible" (apparent or claimed) would fit the assumed purpose, not the displays themselves.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Fossil pollen resembling that of early magnolias has turned up in 95-million-year-old sediments from a single drill core in southern Patagonia. Some paleobotanists caution that the find offers only ______ evidence that flowering plants had reached the region by then: a lone sample could reflect contamination from younger layers, and no other core from the area has yet yielded similar grains.
explanation: The researchers "caution" and then say the sample "could" be contaminated. The evidence is weak but not ruled out. "Tenuous" means slight or flimsy, which is the right strength for a hedged warning.

A.why: "Incontrovertible" means impossible to dispute. The whole sentence is about how the evidence could be disputed.

B.why: "Tangential" means only loosely related. The pollen bears directly on the question; the worry is about how reliable it is, not whether it's relevant.

D.why: "Spurious" means false or not genuine. The researchers say only that contamination is possible ("could reflect"), not that the find is fake. You chose a word stronger than the hedged sentence supports.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Folklorist Nell Ashby calls the "stolen supper" tale strikingly ______. Among the versions she recorded from storytellers in eastern Kentucky, the trickster's name, the animal he outwits, and even whether he escapes unpunished all changed from one teller to the next; only the central ruse, in which he convinces his victim that the food is poisoned, stayed fixed.
explanation: The next sentence defines the label: names, characters, and endings keep changing while one core element stays the same. "Protean" means able to take many forms, which fits a tale that shifts with every teller. Don't pass over it because it's less familiar.

A.why: "Apocryphal" means of doubtful authenticity. It fits the folklore topic, but Ashby says nothing about whether the tale is true or genuine, only that it varies. You matched the subject area instead of the logic.

B.why: "Immutable" means unchanging. Only the central ruse stays fixed, and the passage stresses how much else changes, so this reverses Ashby's point.

C.why: "Anachronistic" means out of its proper time period. Nothing in the passage is about chronology. The variation it describes is from teller to teller, not across eras.
